Diego Ramos: Quick one  I had to leave today for an unexpected medical appointment. I logged it as sick leave but my manager suggested I convert to PTO so it doesn't affect short-term disability eligibility. Is retroactive conversion allowed?

Marta Lopez: Short answer: yes, in limited cases. We allow retroactive sick->PTO conversions up to 14 days after the event for non-claimable absences. If the employee has already submitted a medical claim or a doctors note that triggers an STD claim, we do NOT convert. Need manager attestation + payroll approval.

Anya Singh: Also add: if the sick day was during a release blackout, conversion requires eng lead ack so we can check coverage impact.

Diego Ramos: What evidence do you need for conversion? I can add a manager note that I left early and a short explanation.

Marta Lopez: Required: manager approval (comment), employee statement, and a conversion code on the payroll payload. Optional: medical note (but that will block conversion if its a claim). We'll publish an FAQ entry with examples.

payroll-bot: Reminder: payroll rules -> `retro_conversion_allowed=true` for up to 14 days; if `medical_claim=true` then `retro_conversion_allowed=false`. Payroll needs `payroll_tag` set to `pto_conversion` and `original_absence_type` preserved.

people-ops-bot: Suggested command for retro conversion: `@people-ops-bot convert-sick-to-pto --date 2026-07-14 --reason "personal choice, no claim" --manager=@anya`

Anya Singh: I can approve Diegos conversion. Ill post a brief attestation message in the thread.

Diego Ramos: Thanks. Anything else I need to do?

Marta Lopez: Please confirm you did NOT file a medical claim. If you did, we must keep it as sick. Also confirm whether you want carryover used first. If you prefer to preserve carryover, include `--prefer-current-year` in the command.

Diego Ramos: Confirmed no claim. Also prefer to use carryover days first.

Anya Singh: Approving conversion for 2026-07-14. Manager note: "Observed early departure for appointment; employee requests PTO conversion, no claim filed."

people-ops-bot: Conversion request received. Pre-check: date 2026-07-14 not in global blackout. Manager approval: present. Medical claim flag: false. Payroll payload ready. Reply `confirm` to finalize.

Diego Ramos: confirm

payroll-bot: Payroll payload emitted:
```
employee: diego.ramos
original_date: 2026-07-14
original_type: sick
converted_type: pto
conversion_reason: "personal choice - no claim"
manager_attestation: "Observed early departure; manager approves."
payroll_tag: pto_conversion
use_carryover_first: true
audit_id: pc-2203337777-1
```

Marta Lopez: Logged the conversion in audit and forwarded to payroll for processing. Note for docs: policy bullet we'll add - "Employees may request retroactive conversion of sick to PTO within 14 days if no medical claim has been filed; manager attestation required; payroll will tag the conversion. Conversions during blackout weeks require eng lead approval."

Anya Singh: One edge-case: if the converted PTO pushes someone over the carryover cap for the year, payroll should flag and offer options (pay out vs forfeit vs move to next year) - notify me if that occurs.

Marta Lopez: Good catch, we'll add that automation.

Diego Ramos: Thanks all  cleared up. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

people-ops-bot: Note: thread closed for action. Documentation update assigned to Marta; reminder scheduled for Monday to publish FAQ."
